newsitem.title: USA: Gore reminisces fondly about his presidency.
newsitem.headline: Gore reminisces fondly about his presidency.

text.p: Vice President Al Gore waxed nostalgic on Friday about that time he was the president of the United States.
Gore was not dreaming but merely reminiscing about his five minutes in history on Jan. 20 when he was sworn into office for a second term as vice president before President Bill Clinton was sworn in.
Under the U.S. Constitution, the term of a president begins at noon on Jan. 20 of the year following the presidential election.
But this year Clinton did not take the oath of office for a second term until 12:05 p.m., a delay that sometimes happens during crowded inaugural schedules.

So while most experts agree Clinton was president at noon, those five minutes could be heady stuff for a vice president -- a blink of a presidential era that Gore milked for laughs before the Conference of State Legislators meeting.
"It was a very important five minutes for me," Gore said in his sober-faced manner. "For my family, and, if I may be so bold -- for America."
"A lot of people did overlook my five minutes," Gore continued.
"It might not have been morning in America," he said. "But 12:01 p.m. is pretty close to that."
He told his audience of state officials as they roared with laughter that "historians will remember the Gore administration."
"It was a time when America was at peace," he said.
"Our economy was booming with low inflation -- we created 3.1 jobs." he said with a straight face.
"There were fewer crimes committed in the Gore administration," he noted.

"There were a couple of things important to me, and I say this to a distinguised bipartisan group that knows of the debilitating consequences of a partisan victory -- we've had that all too often in Washington," he said.

"During the Gore administration, during the entire Gore administration, partisan bickering gave forth to bipartisan harmony. Patriotic hymns burst forth for the entire time and I'm especially proud that during my entire term of office I did not ... limit the flexibility of state legislators."

Friday's appearance brought a relaxing few moments for Gore, who answered no questions. He has been in the hot seat all week over his admission that he made questionable telephone calls in 1995 from his White House office soliciting money for Democrats.
